title: Haghtanak (Victory) Bridge
visualBrief: Medium-fi Victory Bridge exterior: three basalt arches, three transverse vault units, six open spandrels per span, four approach passages, simplified intersecting-circle iron lattice, three-globe lamps and six-lane road markings. Detailed original master remains independently reproducible.

nativeAxes.x: southeast along bridge toward Mashtots/Noy end
nativeAxes.y: up from lowest pier foundations at gorge level

sourceFacts.construction: Monolithic reinforced concrete, smooth basalt arch cladding, rough basalt piers and edges, cast-iron handrails; official city inventory.
sourceFacts.reviewScope: Original3448236-triangle/324374144-byte detailed master reproduced exactly; independent medium-fi derivative keeps major arches, open spandrels, transverse units, lattice impressions and lamps, with shared textures instead of individually modeled masonry.

reconstruction.planBasis: Mapped outline about 190 by 30 m; short approach tails extend overall length to 200 m. Three-part transverse piers and paired arch/spandrel forms are interpreted from primary photographs; no survey drawing is asserted.
reconstruction.widthBasis: Published city width 25 m is retained as carriageway reconstruction; mapped full 30 m width includes sidewalks. Neither is silently substituted for the other.

geographicProposal.notes: Inspected pictures confirm three main basalt arches, open spandrels, lattice iron railings and globe lamps. The retained mapped190×30m bridge outline and current standard viewer PMTiles named Victory Bridge roads establish the centre and southeast-facing native+X. Approximate nativebase929.3304m uses the western approach PMTiles sample963.3304m at road modelY34; the opposite approach differs1.4m. Coarse central terrain is about22m above that inferred base and does not resolve the lower gorge. A bounded ground opening below the interior bridge preserves visible vaults while the original PMTiles surroundings remain; this is an approximate visualization, not a surveyed canyon or road endpoint certification. The preview grades only a bounded under-bridge corridor to the inferred gorge base; raw terrain-review and pmtiles-fit samples remain preserved and this is not source bathymetry.

geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry. No downloaded meshes or embedded photographs.
sourceLicense: Repository license for original geometry; map-derived plan © OpenStreetMap contributors ODbL-1.0; reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs with metric UV repeats and per-component vertex tints; separate transparent glazing; no model-specific bitmap textures.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; current renders and geographic fit require review

appearance.identity: Three dark basalt arches, open spandrels and ornate iron railing; current exterior.
appearance.exclusions: Precise canyon floor, traffic and engineering certification.

limitations: Approximate picture/PMTiles exterior and orientation fit; no bespoke survey or local-data research.

Original detailed324MB master is preserved by its unchanged recipe/map inputs and exact reproduced hash. Independent medium-fi source replaces modeled masonry courses with shared basalt texture, simplifies the intersecting-circle cast iron and retains main/spandrel/approach openings, transverse units and lamps. Browser levels reduce these further.

PMTiles western approach anchors the road at modelY34; coarse under-bridge terrain does not resolve the canyon. Bounded ground opening is a visualization approximation. Precise river, bank walls and endpoint joins are not certified. Footprint replacement off; physical-device timing remains pending.
importReason: Preserve thin cables, rail frames and hardware across the full crossing; whole-object quantization loses these details.
